title: Response Period and Documents Due Date on a Patient Financial Assistance Program Documents Request
content:
**Rule.** Under the Patient Financial Assistance Program, an application that needs documents and lacks them is set to pending documents with a documents due date that falls the response days after the request date. The response days are the tier's documents due days, counted in calendar days from the request date as day 0.

**The document period.** The document period runs from the request date, counted as day 0, through the documents due date the case records, including any extension granted, and a denial for missing documents is allowed only from the day after that date.

## Counting from day 0

The request date is day 0. The first calendar day after it is day 1, and the documents due date is the day whose number equals the response days. The case's documents due date, as recorded on the case, is the last day of the document period.

## Illustration (hypothetical figure of 20 response days, used here only to show the count)

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Documents requested (day 0) | Monday 4 May 2026 |
| Day 1 | Tuesday 5 May 2026 |
| Documents due date (day 20) | Sunday 24 May 2026 |
| Last day of the document period | Sunday 24 May 2026 |
| First day a denial for missing documents is allowed | Monday 25 May 2026 |

If the case later records an extended documents due date of 8 June 2026, the document period runs through 8 June 2026 and a denial for missing documents is allowed only from 9 June 2026.

## Boundary readings

- On the documents due date itself the period has not ended; a denial for missing documents is not allowed that day.
- The day after the recorded documents due date, a denial for missing documents is allowed.
